provenance.authorship: Original project scenario, AI-assisted draft. Practitioner review and scoring calibration pending.

title: Experienced Manager: Repair a Hiring Debrief
prompt: Review this fictional hiring debrief for a team supervisor: Candidate A scored 4/5 on a scheduling exercise and 2/5 on a coaching exercise; Candidate B scored 3/5 and 4/5. The role requires both. One panelist says, "A feels like us; I want someone I could have a drink with." Another proposes adding a surprise unpaid assignment only for B. No final decision has been made. Explain how you would lead the debrief.

rubric.label: Keep criteria job-relevant
rubric.description: Uses agreed criteria instead of similarity.

anchors.0: Uses social similarity or presumed background as the selection reason.
anchors.2: Rejects the similarity comment and returns to the two skills.
anchors.4: Uses the pre-agreed equal weighting, avoids inventing a retrospective threshold and distinguishes evidence for scheduling from evidence for coaching.

rubric.label: Examine rating support
rubric.description: Handles missing evidence before treating scores as facts.

anchors.0: Treats unsupported scores or confidence as sufficient proof.
anchors.4: Checks the unsupported coaching score, records uncertainty and seeks comparable clarification where justified instead of selectively adding burdens to one candidate.

rubric.label: Lead a consistent debrief
rubric.description: Establishes an accountable and fair next step.

anchors.0: Allows different unplanned tasks for one candidate or claims the arithmetic alone proves who must be hired.
anchors.2: Proposes a consistent follow-up and documented decision.
anchors.4: Separates discussion of each criterion, invites dissenting evidence, follows the authorized same-standard clarification route and documents the final reasoning and limits.

reference.scenario: Review this fictional hiring debrief for a team supervisor: Candidate A scored 4/5 on a scheduling exercise and 2/5 on a coaching exercise; Candidate B scored 3/5 and 4/5. The role requires both. One panelist says, "A feels like us; I want someone I could have a drink with." Another proposes adding a surprise unpaid assignment only for B. No final decision has been made. Explain how you would lead the debrief.

facts.value: The panel agreed before interviews to weight scheduling and coaching equally, but did not define a minimum score. One assessor’s coaching notes for A contain no quoted or described behavior.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about agreed criteria or evidence quality

facts.value: Both candidates completed the same tasks. A comparable short clarification can be offered to both if the hiring owner approves; the panel must not invent a new criterion after seeing candidates.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about a fair way to resolve missing evidence

model_points: Uses the pre-agreed equal weighting, avoids inventing a retrospective threshold and distinguishes evidence for scheduling from evidence for coaching.
Checks the unsupported coaching score, records uncertainty and seeks comparable clarification where justified instead of selectively adding burdens to one candidate.
Separates discussion of each criterion, invites dissenting evidence, follows the authorized same-standard clarification route and documents the final reasoning and limits.

probes.trigger: candidate selects B immediately from averages
probes.question: Which rating lacks evidence, and how does that affect your confidence?

probes.trigger: candidate proposes another test for just one candidate
probes.question: How would you keep the comparison consistent?
What changed in your evidence rather than your preference?

fair_alternatives: The panel may decide on existing evidence if its limits are acknowledged and the authorized hiring owner accepts them.
A structured clarification is not automatically required; it must be proportionate and comparable.
reference.assessment_limits: Assess only the decisions and reasoning demonstrated in this fictional exercise. No hiring-readiness, personality, legal compliance or workplace performance claim follows from this score. A valid alternative can earn full credit. Unrevealed conditional facts must not be assumed known or required for credit; credit asking for needed information and a conditional plan.

interviewer_notes: You are the counterpart named in the prompt. If this is a written review, remain the hiring interviewer while the candidate reads and writes. Let the candidate finish, including thinking and self-correction. Answer only supplied facts when their reveal condition is met; otherwise say the information is unknown. Use neutral probes after a completed answer, one at a time. Do not prescribe the rubric as a spoken checklist. Accept relevant examples from work, education and community leadership. Do not request private employee records, infer protected traits, invent employment rules or promise a real organizational outcome. Simulation gives no answer before assessment; coaching may offer labeled assistance.

learning_drills.title: Rewrite a hiring debrief
learning_drills.prompt: Rewrite the two panel comments as requests for observable evidence and a consistent next step. This is self-guided practice with no automated assessment.
